mainTopic: Which כהנים receive חרמים and fields, and the משנה on חרמי כהנים, unspecified חרמים, and making a חרם of קדשים
overview: The גמרא finishes a list of rules about which כהנים receive holy property. Plain חרמים may go to any כהן, but a field made חרם goes to the כהן of the משמר serving right now. This is learned through a גזרה שוה from גזל הגר, and a ברייתא shows where גזל הגר itself gets this rule. A field that passes to the כהנים at the יובל goes to the משמר serving when the יובל begins. If that happens on שבת, it goes to the outgoing משמר, and a ברייתא about יובל and שמיטה cancelling at the same moment supports this. Next, חזקיה בר בילוטי asks why movables are not compared to land. רבי אבהו answers that this comparison is a dispute between תנאים. A new משנה then teaches that חרמי כהנים cannot be redeemed, and records the dispute over where an unspecified חרם goes. It ends by explaining how a person can make a חרם of his own קרבנות and of a בכור, and how the payment is measured.

steps.title: A field made חרם goes to the כהן of the serving משמר
steps.stepSummary: Regular חרמים go to any כהן, but a field made חרם goes to the כהן of the משמר on duty. This is learned from the word 'לכהן' that also appears in גזל הגר.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...shall be yours.' If someone made his fields חרם, he gives them to the כהן of the משמר serving then. The פסוק says: 'As a field of חרם, its possession shall be to the כהן.' We learn the word 'to the כהן' here from the same words in the case of robbing a convert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the source for regular חרמים, which go to any כהן. Then it gives a special rule for fields made חרם: they go to the כהן of the משמר serving at that time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular חרמים can be given to any כהן the owner chooses. A field is different, and the גמרא learns this through a גזרה שוה: 'לכהן' in the פסוק about fields matches 'לכהן' in the פסוק about גזל הגר. Whatever is true there, going to the serving משמר, is true here too.

steps.title: Where do we know the rule for robbery of a convert?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that גזל הגר goes to the serving משמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, in the case of robbing a convert, how do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where גזל הגר itself gets the rule of going to the serving משמר. This sets up the next step, where a ברייתא answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule for fields was learned from גזל הגר. That only works if גזל הגר has a clear source of its own. So the גמרא checks the foundation.

steps.title: A ברייתא‎: ה׳ acquires it and gives it to the serving כהן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'לה' לכהן' to mean that ה׳ acquires the payment and gives it to the כהן of the משמר on duty.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'To ה׳, to the כהן' means ה׳ acquired it and gave it to the כהן of that משמר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא explains the פסוק about גזל הגר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the payment is 'לה'' (to ה׳) and then 'לכהן' (to the כהן). The ברייתא reads this as a two-stage handover: ה׳ first acquires it, then passes it to the כהן serving at that time.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To ה׳, to the כהן,' words from במדבר 5:8
ה׳ acquired it

steps.title: Maybe it can go to any כהן he wants?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges its own reading: perhaps the payment may go to any כהן at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it goes to the כהן of that משמר? Or maybe it can go to any כהן he wants?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own explanation. Perhaps 'לכהן' just means any כהן the robber chooses. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לכהן' alone do not say which כהן. Plain חרמים, for example, can go to any כהן. So the ברייתא needs to show why this case is limited to the serving משמר.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only…, a phrase that raises another possible reading
Whom he wants

phrases.english: You say to the priest of that watch,
or is it perhaps only

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'לכהן' means the כהן of the serving משמר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'לכהן' could just as easily mean any כהן at all.

steps.title: Proof from the איל הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק mentions the אשם ram offered for atonement, so it is speaking about the כהן who is serving and offering קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says, 'Besides the ram of atonement through which he will atone for him,' this shows the פסוק is talking about the כהן of that משמר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own challenge. It proves from later words in the same פסוק that the payment goes to the serving משמר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the payment to the כהן who offers the atonement ram. The כהן who offers קרבנות is the one on duty in the מקדש. So 'לכהן' here means a כהן of the serving משמר, not any כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: The ram of atonement, the אשם brought with the payment
He will bring atonement
The פסוק is speaking about

steps.whatToRemember: גזל הגר goes to the serving משמר because the same פסוק ties it to the כהן offering the atonement ram. Fields made חרם share this rule through the matching word 'לכהן'.

phrases.english: When it says:

steps.title: A field leaving at the יובל goes to the משמר on duty then
steps.stepSummary: A consecrated field that passes to the כהנים at the יובל goes to the משמר serving when the יובל begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: A field that goes out to the כהנים at the יובל is given to the משמר that is serving when the יובל arrives.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule about property given to the כהנים: a field that passes to them at the יובל goes to the משמר serving at the moment the יובל begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the question is not 'which כהן?' but 'which week's group?'. The answer is tied to timing: the moment the יובל starts decides which משמר receives the field.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A field passing to the כהנים at the יובל goes to the משמר serving when the יובל begins.

steps.title: What if the יובל begins on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask what happens if the יובל begins on שבת, when one משמר leaves and the next one comes in.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if the יובל began on שבת, what is the rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about the rule just given. If the יובל starts on שבת, two משמרות are present, so which one gets the field? The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משמרות switch on שבת, so on that day the leaving group and the arriving group are both in the מקדש. The rule 'the משמר serving when the יובל begins' no longer points clearly to one group.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them
What is the rule?

steps.confusionAlert: שבת matters here because it is the day the משמרות change over, so two groups are in the מקדש at once.

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
If it arrived on Shabbat, what is the rule?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ פָּגַע בּוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about an unclear case within the rule of step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which משמר gets the field when the יובל begins on שבת, the changeover day

steps.title: It goes to the leaving משמר
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אמי, quoting חולפנא, rules that the field goes to the משמר that is leaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אמי said in the name of חולפנא: he gives it to the משמר that is leaving.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered. On the changeover שבת, the field goes to the outgoing משמר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of the two groups present on that שבת, the one finishing its week receives the field. This settles the unclear case raised in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: The outgoing watch, the group finishing its week of service
He gives it

steps.whatToRemember: A field leaving at the יובל goes to the משמר on duty when the יובל begins. If that happens on the changeover שבת, it goes to the outgoing משמר.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Ami said
in the name of Ḥulfana:
One gives it to the watch that is leaving.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּחוּלְפָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The field is given to the outgoing משמר.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that יובל and שמיטה cancel at the same moment
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק cites a ברייתא: יובל and שמיטה cancel together, since יובל works at its start and שמיטה at its end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: A ברייתא teaches that it turns out יובל and שמיטה both cancel at the same moment. יובל cancels at its beginning, and שמיטה cancels at its end.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a ברייתא that supports the ruling that the field goes to the משמר that is leaving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the שמיטה year (year 49) and the start of the יובל year (year 50) are the same moment. So יובל takes effect right as the old year ends, on the evening of ראש השנה. At that moment the משמר that served on שבת has not yet left, because the משמרות switch only in the morning.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year of the cycle, when debts are cancelled
They cancel or release (debts, sales)
It turns out that you can say

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the field question to the exact moment יובל begins, which decides which משמר gets the field.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: תַּנְיָא,
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: It is taught in a baraita,
you turn out to be saying,
both the Jubilee and the Sabbatical Year
cancel at the same time,
phrases.notes: Literally "as one." Year 49 ends at the same moment year 50 begins.

phrases.english: except that the Jubilee does so at its beginning
and the Sabbatical Year at its end.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support the ruling of step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that the field goes to the outgoing משמר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that יובל and שמיטה cancel at the same moment.

steps.title: Questioning the word "except" in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that "except that" is the wrong word, because this is exactly the reason they cancel together.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, it is because of this!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Except that" sounds like a limit on the rule. But יובל starting at its beginning and שמיטה ending at its end is not a limit. It is the very reason both cancel at the same moment.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Because of this

phrases.english: On the contrary, it is because of that!
phrases.notes: He means: יובל starting at its beginning is the reason they line up, not something that goes against it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase "אלא ש" (except that) in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The beginning/end timing explains why they cancel together. It is not an exception to the rule.

steps.title: Read it as "because" instead of "except"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: say "because the יובל...".
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: Because the יובל cancels at its beginning, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the wording problem by changing "except that" to "because."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא reads smoothly: they cancel at the same moment because יובל works at its start and שמיטה at its end. The ruling itself does not change. Only the wording is fixed.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (read the text this way)
Because

phrases.english: Say: Because the Jubilee, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." stands for the rest of the line: "at its beginning and the שמיטה at its end."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא presents the timing as an exception.
steps.terutzMaskana: The timing is the reason both cancel together.

steps.title: Doesn't יובל start on יום הכיפורים?
steps.stepSummary: שמיטה ending at its end fits the פסוק. But the פסוק puts יובל on יום הכיפורים, not at the very start of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that שמיטה cancels at its end, since it says "At the end of seven years you shall make a release." But does יובל cancel at its beginning? It happens on יום הכיפורים, as it says: "On יום הכיפורים you shall sound the שופר throughout your land"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's claim that יובל takes effect at the very start of the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שמיטה part fits its פסוק. But the פסוק links יובל to the שופר on יום הכיפורים, ten days into the year. If so, יובל would not line up with the end of שמיטה, and the support for step 8 seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that (granted)
At the end of
The Day of Atonement, the 10th of תשרי
You shall sound the שופר

phrases.english: Granted, the Sabbatical Year cancels at its end,
as it is written: “At the end of seven years you shall make a release,”
phrases.notes: דברים 15:1

phrases.english: but does the Jubilee cancel at its beginning?
It is on Yom Kippur,
as it is written: “On Yom Kippur
you shall sound the shofar throughout all your land”!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what the ברייתא in step 9 says about when יובל starts.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that יובל cancels at its beginning (ראש השנה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק ties יובל to יום הכיפורים, ten days after the year begins.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה
steps.stepSummary: This ברייתא follows the view that יובל takes effect from ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, who says that יובל takes effect from ראש השנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by naming a תנא who holds that יובל starts on ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, יובל already takes effect on ראש השנה, and the שופר on יום הכיפורים does not change that. So the ברייתא is correct by his view, and the support for the outgoing משמר still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
Takes effect
The New Year, the 1st of תשרי

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא, and the support it gives to the outgoing משמר, follows the view that יובל takes effect on ראש השנה.

phrases.english: Whose view is this?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הִיא,
phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka,
who says: It is from Rosh HaShana
that the Jubilee takes effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Naming which תנא the ברייתא follows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יובל only takes effect on יום הכיפורים.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, יובל takes effect from ראש השנה.

steps.title: Shouldn't movable property be compared to land?
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה בר בילוטי raises a challenge before רבי אבהו against the earlier ruling: movable property should follow the same rule as land.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה בר בילוטי heard this and went and said before רבי אבהו: But let us compare movable property to land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge to the rule that movable things given to כהנים may go to any כהן, while land goes to the serving משמר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about dedicating things lists movable things together with a field. So חזקיה argues that the two should be compared, and movable property should also go to the serving משמר, just like land.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us compare (link two things listed together in a פסוק)
Movable property
Land

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya bar Biluti heard it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the earlier ruling: movable property may go to any כהן, but land goes to the serving משמר.

phrases.english: and went and said before Rabbi Abbahu:
But let one compare movable property to land!
phrases.notes: The פסוק he has in mind is ויקרא 27:28, which lists movable things and a field together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the rule about movable property versus land and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference between movable property (any כהן) and land (the serving משמר).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק links the two, so they should follow the same rule.

steps.title: Comparing movables to land is a dispute, and this ruling follows the side that does not compare
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that whether movables are compared to land is a dispute between תנאים, and the ruling follows the view that does not compare them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a dispute between תנאים? Some compare movable property to land and some do not. This ruling follows the one who says we do not compare them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers חזקיה בר בילוטי's challenge from Step 14. Not everyone agrees that movable property must follow the rule for land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה בר בילוטי assumed movables must follow the same law as land. רבי אבהו points out that this comparison (הקש) is itself a dispute between תנאים, as the גמרא showed earlier. The ruling simply follows the side that does not make the comparison, so the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: תנאים: the sages of the משנה era. 'A dispute of תנאים' means earlier authorities already argued about this.
Compares, using a הקש: linking two things so the law of one applies to the other.
We do not make the comparison.

steps.whatToRemember: A challenge built on an assumed comparison is answered by showing that the comparison itself is disputed, and the ruling follows the side that rejects it.

phrases.english: Is it not a dispute between תנאים?
For there is one who compares,
phrases.notes: He means comparing movable property to land, as the גמרא discussed earlier.

phrases.english: and there is one who does not compare.
This ruling is like the one who says, "We do not compare."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the challenger's assumption is itself a dispute between תנאים and assigns the ruling to the other side.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Movable property must follow the same rule as land.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some תנאים do not compare movables to land, and the ruling follows them.

steps.title: Property dedicated to priests cannot be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that חרמי כהנים have no redemption and are given to the כהנים like תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Property dedicated to the כהנים cannot be redeemed. Instead, it is given to the כהנים, just like תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that something dedicated as a חרם for the כהנים cannot be bought back. It simply goes to the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other dedications, such as gifts to בדק הבית, can be redeemed with money. חרמי כהנים cannot. They become the כהנים' own property, the same way תרומה does.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of a new משנה.
Property dedicated as a חרם for the כהנים.
Redemption: buying a dedicated item back with money.
The gift of produce given to a כהן, which becomes his own property.

phrases.english: MISHNA
Dedications for priests have no redemption;
rather, they are given to the priests like תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חרמי כהנים cannot be redeemed and are given to the כהנים like תרומה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בתירא: an unspecified dedication goes to Temple upkeep
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא holds that a סתם חרם goes to בדק הבית, based on the פסוק 'כל חרם קדש קדשים הוא לה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: a dedication made without saying its purpose goes to בדק הבית, as the פסוק says, "Every dedicated item is most sacred to ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings the first opinion about a חרם where the person did not say whom it is for. רבי יהודה בן בתירא says it goes to the upkeep of the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof is the phrase 'לה׳' (to ה׳) in the פסוק. He reads it as meaning the item belongs to the הקדש treasury, not to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Dedications made without stating their purpose.
Upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש.
Most holy.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
Unspecified dedications go to Temple upkeep,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כׇּל חֵרֶם קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים הוּא לַה׳״.
phrases.english: as it is stated: "Every dedicated item is most sacred to the Lord."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:28

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the first opinion on the case of an unspecified חרם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סתם חרם goes to בדק הבית.

steps.title: חכמים: an unspecified dedication goes to the priests
steps.stepSummary: חכמים hold that a סתם חרם goes to the כהנים, based on the פסוק 'כשדה החרם לכהן תהיה אחזתו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים say: a dedication made without saying its purpose goes to the כהנים, as the פסוק says, "Like a dedicated field, its possession shall be the כהן's."
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה בן בתירא. They say an unspecified חרם goes to the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their proof is a פסוק that calls a field a 'שדה החרם' and gives it to the כהן. This shows that a plain חרם belongs to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: A field that has been dedicated as a חרם.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
Unspecified dedications go to the priests,
as it is stated: "Like a dedicated field,
its possession shall be the priest's."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:21

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סתם חרם goes to the כהנים.

steps.title: Then what does 'every dedicated item is most sacred to ה׳' teach?
steps.stepSummary: חכמים raise the obvious question against themselves: if a חרם goes to the כהנים, what is the purpose of רבי יהודה בן בתירא's פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say, "Every dedicated item is most sacred to ה׳"?
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים raise a question against their own view. If a חרם goes to the כהנים, what is the other פסוק there for? This sets up their answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן בתירא used this פסוק as his proof. חכמים must show that it teaches something else, otherwise it would seem to support him.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if your view is correct.
Why was it stated? It asks what a פסוק comes to teach.

phrases.english: If so, why is it stated:
"Every dedicated item is most sacred to the Lord"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Addresses the opposing proof-text from inside the חכמים' view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' view that a סתם חרם goes to the כהנים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק 'לה׳' seems to send a חרם to הקדש, so the חכמים must explain what it means.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches that חרם takes effect even on offerings
steps.stepSummary: חכמים explain that the פסוק teaches that a חרם can take effect on both קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that a חרם takes effect on קדשי קדשים and on קדשים קלים.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים answer their question. The פסוק is not about where a חרם goes. It teaches that a person can make a חרם even on things that are already קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'קדש קדשים' in the פסוק are read as a hint to offerings. So even an animal already set aside as a קרבן, whether of high or lower holiness, can be made a חרם. This removes the פסוק as proof for רבי יהודה בן בתירא.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the most holy level (for example עולה, חטאת).
Offerings of lesser holiness (for example שלמים).
Takes effect.

phrases.english: That it takes effect on offerings of the most sacred order
and on offerings of lesser sanctity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the פסוק to teach a different law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק 'לה׳' means a חרם goes to הקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that a חרם takes effect even on קדשים of both levels.

steps.title: Dedicating one's own offerings: for a vowed offering, he gives their value
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a person may make a חרם of his own קדשים, and if the offering came from a נדר, he gives its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may dedicate his own offerings as a חרם, both the most holy ones and those of lesser holiness. If the offering came from a נדר, he gives their value.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now explains how the rule from Step 20 works in practice, starting with an offering that came from a נדר. The next step gives the rule for a נדבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a חרם takes effect on קדשים, the משנה describes what the owner must do. If the offering came from a נדר, he does not give the animal itself. He gives its monetary value.

keyTerms.meaning: Dedicates as a חרם.
A vow, for example 'I take upon myself to bring an עולה'.
Their value or worth in money.

steps.confusionAlert: The animal itself is not handed over to the כהן. For a vowed offering, the owner gives its value.

phrases.english: A person may dedicate his sacrificial animals,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים בֵּין קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים,
phrases.english: both offerings of the most sacred order and offerings of lesser sanctity.
If it was a vow, he gives their value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the rule of Step 20 is carried out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may make a חרם of his own קדשים, and for an offering from a נדר he gives its value.

steps.title: A gift offering: he pays only the value of his stake in it
steps.stepSummary: If the קרבן he made a חרם was a נדבה, he pays only its טובה, meaning his personal stake in it. For example, with 'This bull is an עולה' we estimate what a person would pay for the right to offer this bull as his own עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it was a gift offering, he pays the value of his personal benefit in it. For example, if he said 'This bull is a burnt offering,' we estimate how much a person would pay for this bull so he could offer it as his own burnt offering, even though he isn't really allowed to do so.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues from step 21. After the case of a נדר, it now gives the rule for a נדבה and shows how to measure the payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a נדר ('I take upon myself an עולה') the owner must replace the animal if it is lost, so it is almost like his own money, and he pays its full value. With a נדבה ('this animal is an עולה') he owes nothing if it is lost, so all he has left is a small stake: the benefit of being the one who brings it. That stake is what he pays when he makes it a חרם.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift offering where the person says 'this animal' is a קרבן. He is not responsible to replace it.
Their benefit: the owner's own small stake in the קרבן
A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
We estimate the price
Permitted, allowed

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up נדר and נדבה here. A נדר means paying the animal's full value (step 21). A נדבה means paying only the owner's small personal stake.

phrases.english: And if it was a gift offering,
he gives the value of his benefit in them.
phrases.notes: The 'benefit' is the owner's own stake in the animal. The next lines show how to put a price on it.

phrases.english: "This bull is a burnt offering" —
we estimate how much a person would want to give
for this bull, in order to offer it up as a burnt offering,
even though he is not permitted to.
phrases.notes: This is only an imagined price. We picture the deal just to put a number on the owner's stake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the rule from step 21 by giving the other side: a נדבה instead of a נדר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a נדבה made into a חרם, the owner pays only his stake in it: what someone would pay to offer that animal as his own עולה.

steps.title: A firstborn animal can be made a חרם
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a בכור, whether תם or בעל מום, can be made a חרם.
steps.simpleTranslation: A firstborn animal, whether it is unblemished or blemished, can be declared a חרם.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a new case: a בכור animal. It rules that a בכור can also be made a חרם, whether it is perfect or blemished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור must go to a כהן, so it might seem the owner has nothing left to make a חרם from. The משנה says he still can, in both cases: when the animal is fit for the מזבח (תם) and when it is blemished (בעל מום). This sets up the next question: how much is it worth?

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male animal, which is given to a כהן
Unblemished, fit to be brought as a קרבן
Blemished, not fit for the מזבח
They may declare it a חרם

phrases.english: The firstborn animal,
whether unblemished or blemished —
one may declare it a חרם,

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבְּכוֹר, בֵּין תָּם בֵּין בַּעַל מוּם — מַחְרִימִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another kind of holy animal, a בכור, to the list of things one can make a חרם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור, whether תם or בעל מום, can be made a חרם.

steps.title: How do we price the firstborn?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how the redemption payment for a בכור made into a חרם is measured.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we redeem it?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a quick question to set up its next line: how much does the owner pay?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור already belongs to the כהנים in general, so its value to the owner isn't obvious. The משנה asks how to measure the payment, and answers in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: How?
Redeem: pay money to release it from the חרם

phrases.english: And how does one redeem it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 23's ruling by asking how the payment is measured.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the value of a בכור made into a חרם is measured

steps.title: Price it by what someone would pay to give it to a relative כהן
steps.stepSummary: We estimate what a person would pay for the right to give this בכור to a כהן who is his daughter's son or his sister's son.
steps.simpleTranslation: We estimate how much a person would be willing to pay for this firstborn in order to give it to his daughter's son or his sister's son.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its question. The owner's stake in a בכור is his right to choose which כהן gets it, and we put a price on that right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner can't keep a בכור, but he does get to decide which כהן receives it. Someone with a כהן grandson or nephew would gladly pay for that choice. That amount is what the owner pays, like the 'benefit' value of the נדבה in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: His daughter's son
His sister's son

steps.whatToRemember: When someone makes a חרם of a holy item he can't fully own (a נדבה or a בכור), he pays only the value of his own small stake in it. That means the benefit of offering it, or the right to choose which כהן gets it.

phrases.english: We estimate how much a person would want to give
for this firstborn
to give it to his daughter's son
phrases.notes: Here the grandson is a כהן, so this person would pay for the right to send the בכור to him.

phrases.english: or to his sister's son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹמְדִין כַּמָּה אָדָם רוֹצֶה לִיתֵּן בִּבְכוֹר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The payment is what a person would give for the right to hand the בכור to a כהן relative (his daughter's son or sister's son).
